title: Service Contracts: Holding Contracts on Several Trade Lanes
content:
AHL Service Contracts are written lane by lane. This card states how many of them one customer may hold side by side.

## Clause

A single customer may be party to several Service Contracts at once, each covering its own trade lane. The line sets no maximum on the number of lanes a customer may contract on, and so no maximum on the number of contracts it may hold across lanes.

How the contracts on different lanes are taken together — for example when they are counted as a portfolio — is a separate matter of portfolio aggregation and is not decided by this clause.

## At a glance

| Point | Position |
|---|---|
| Contracts per trade lane under this clause | one |
| Ceiling on the number of lanes (and contracts) per customer | none set |

## Points of judgement

**Does a contract a customer already holds on one lane limit what it may hold elsewhere?** Not by number: each lane carries its own contract, and the count of lanes is uncapped.

**Is there a figure beyond which a customer holds too many Service Contracts?** No such figure exists in the policy.
